mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month indicates a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in one month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a weakening in the housing market, which is a significant component of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST declines for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% in one month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity and investment in equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances following a decrease in FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it indicates a tight labor market with high borrowing costs, which typically leads to a slowdown in economic growth and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with low unemployment
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE < 4%.
